item.title: Re: Questionable SCP
item.content:encoded:
"for being overly Judeo-Christian is a good thing"

Got to disagree with you very hard here. Criticism of entries which are just deities for the sake of being deities or, as later headcanons have often rendered 343 here, extremely powerful reality benders, are perfectly valid. But for being "overly Judeo-Christian?" Why? We have multiple SCPs whose lore and mechanics are built on religions, myths and folk-lore from around the world and throughout time, including SCPs based on fictional religions: we've got Abel, Cain, multiple demons, at least one Hindu deity, Sarkic & Mekhanite creatures, etc. The idea that an SCP is suddenly less valid because it's 'overly Judeo-Christian' seems utterly ridiculous: if your concern is that it asserts Christian or generally Abrahamic mythology as being 'real' over others, then I'd tell you to refer to the 'no canon' rule and the hundreds of conflicting SCPs we already have.

item.content:encoded:
I've read this one a couple times over the years, still works as what it is.

One thing I wanted to talk about, though: is Dr. ███████████ even gone? Many comments talk about that, and after checking the edit history the wording has been pretty stable, but it isn't a given.

Points from the text:
-There is no record of Dr. Blackbox working with Dr. Beck or 343
-Staff specifically questioned about the document claim not to have met Dr. Blackbox
-The document data was recovered during a routine check of Dr. Blackbox's drive

These points do not clearly mean that Dr. Blackbox is gone. Point 1 demonstrates that there have been record changes, since we have residual information about the doctor working with Beck and 343, but doesn't say the doctor is gone. Point 3 suggests that the doctor is working somewhere else in the Foundation, as his data was subject to routine check. Point 2 is the most suggestive, but could still be specific to the document. It doesn't say questioned staff are unaware of the doctor's existence, merely that they haven't met the doctor. That could mean asking about the doctor's work with 343 causes the questioned party to forget knowing them.

I suspect the author meant for the doctor to be erased, but that isn't clearly the case in the text. Erasing Dr. ███████████ would be the only documented, clearly evil action by 343, and even that is ambiguous. The other protocol inconsistencies are about bending the Foundation and its personnel to allow 343's continued activity.

This SCP has hung around a long while despite regular criticism, and I'd bet one big reason is that it leaves so much room for interpretation.

Hey, I've seen you posting on several pages with Jewish/Christian/Muslim influences.

If you're interested in SCPs from other religions, try:

SCP-3740, the Assyrian God Ashur,

SCP-4500, involving Greek mythology,

SCP-1846, a Native American corn god,

SCP-029, the avatar of Kali

SCP-722, the Midgar serpent

SCP-208, the Egyptian God Set

SCP-3507, based on Japanese mythology

Most of the religious element was generic Christian when the site started because much of the userbase was generic Christian or Christian-turned-atheist.

But it seems disingenuous to go from article to article complaining about Abrahamic elements, especially when you're picking ones where the connection is really tenuous. SCP-343 certainly doesn't act like the God in the Bible, he's probably just some weird alien warping people's brains.

If you want to complain about Abrahamic stuff, check out SCP-076, SCP-073, and SCP-616. Those are really over the top with the references.

A great Abrahamic one, though, is the Gate Guardian, Dr. Clef's Proposal for SCP-001. You should check it out!

item.title: Longpost is long
item.content:encoded:
There has been much heated discussion about this SCP over the years, many differing opinions on whether the article should be re-written, archived, or just slightly edited.

My opinion may be insignificant, but I still wanted to chime in:
I believe that it should be left as is, with the exception of slight edits to improve readability of some of the clunkier sentences.1

+ My reasoning is as follows:
- This is the short version:

The article and the SCP in question are written to be incredibly ambiguous:

  • It may be God, or maybe not;
  • It may be benevolent, or it maybe evil;
  • It may be trying to help the Foundation, or maybe it's slowly worming it's way inside the system, converting personnel one-by-one into it's puppets;
  • It's classification of "Safe" may have been made after considering empirical data, or maybe the one writing the article is already under "God's" control;
  • The subject of whether Dr. Beck's request to increase staff rotation is odd or not was closed by O5-█ because O5-█ knows something we don't and has decided that it is safe, or maybe no O5 member has actually reviewed the request and the message is a fake… or maybe even O5-█ has fallen under 343's control!
  • Are Dr. Blackbox Blackbox's missing reports/orders the result of Dr. Beck's 343-induced-meddling or is Dr. Beck simply doing it because he believes that it is for the good of the Foundation… or maybe the one who deleted the data is Dr. Blackbox himself?!

Some may say that there's not enough written about 343, that more details should be added, that 343 is one-dimensional and boring.
I say, you're not looking deep enough. The lack of details is the whole point.

Some may say that the SCP Foundation would never classify such an entity as "Safe", that they would never overlook such containment/procedural transgressions.
I say, you are absolutely correct! They never would. And yet this article is the way it is… wouldn't this actually imply that something may be amiss? Or maybe it just happened to slip through multiple checks without anybody noticing… After all, such things happen sometimes… rarely… if ever… God is watching

Footnotes
1. e.g. "In regards to document 343-1a, there are no relevant records available or seemingly in existence and, similarly, all records of Dr. ████████████ ███████████ ever working with SCP-343 or Dr. Beck are missing and presumed non-existent."

item.title: Interesting...
item.content:encoded:
I find the addendums pretty intriguing. If I'm reading them right, then does that mean that SCP-343 has erased Dr. [REDACTED] from existence? The addendum's make a point of showing that Dr. [REDACTED] did exist, but everyone working around 343 or on 343 can't seem to remember Dr. [REDACTED] ever existing. I mean, he clearly did exist since the document references him and his terminal exists. But what I am getting at is that Dr. [REDACTED] confronted SCP-343 about something and now is no longer present in staff memory.

If I am reading this correctly, then this adds a whole different level to this document. This shows that, regardless of if this SCP is God or not, SCP 343 is NOT friendly (despite how hard he tries to act). I mean, if SCP-343 was as beneficial and good as he tries to look, then Dr. [REDACTED] would still be around. That means the SCP Foundation has a powerful reality-bending entity in their midst that is not only uncontainable but also possibly malevolent. Food for thought.

item.title: Possible Rewrite?
item.content:encoded: With classic SCP's being rewritten recently I would really like to see this one be updated. It would interesting if this SCP was proved or strongly implied to be just a reality warper pretending to be God. The SCP claims to be the Abrahamic God, but shows many inconsistencies with said God. For example, this SCP lacks omniscience (has been surprised by Dr. Bright), omnipotence (could not defeat 682), did not create all creatures (did not create 682), and can be physically seen without immediate death. These could be pointed out and further interviews and experiments could be conducted to further flesh out this SCP. It would likely interest more people too as it would explain quite a few things as well as making people wary of future reality warpers. Just a thought though.

item.content:encoded:
Normally I wouldn't be bothered by this, seeing how this was created in Series I. But this strikes me as -ARC writing quality. And, yeah, the idea of a reality bender with a narcissistic disorder is very interesting, but it's done so bad here.

  • The Foundation should take greater measure to contain this thing.
  • The Foundation shouldn't instantly recognize 343 as God.
  • The "data" at the end seems like it's trying to build upon a greater backstory, which I've found is a prevalent trope in bad self-insert scips (although this has been done right before, this instance hasn't been expanded on at all. Plus, it just isn't very gripping to me).
  • The redaction just looks sloppy.

Heritage or not, this is in need of a major rewrite.
